note: Cuba: nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90 days (Russia in 180), 60, 30 or 28; nationals of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Haiti, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and the others listed may not use the e-Visa and need one from a Cuban mission, and Kosovars are refused (taken as a visa). Everyone else gets an e-Visa for 90 days (since August 2024; extendable by 90, not modelled). Benin's agreement exempts only students, so Beninese take the e-Visa; Bosnia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Mongolia and Namibia, whose agreements Timatic still shows, are taken as the e-Visa site has them. Proof of insurance, a return ticket and USD 50 a day are asked of everyone (not modelled). Read from Wikipedia's copy.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Cuba
sources.said: Visitors to Cuba must obtain an e-Visa unless they are citizens from one of the visa-exempt countries or citizens who must obtain a visa from one of the Cuban diplomatic missions . ... Citizens of the following countries may enter Cuba without a visa for the following period: 90 days China Malaysia United Arab Emirates 90 days within any 180 days Russia 60 days Grenada Saint Vincent and the Grenadines 30 days Antigua and Barbuda Belarus Saint Kitts and Nevis Saint Lucia Singapore 28 days Barbados Dominica According to the visa agreement between Benin and Cuba , Beninese students who have an ordinary passport may enter Cuba without a visa for a maximum stay of 90 days. ... but the e-Visa website states that these citizens must apply for an e-Visa. ... Since August 2024, visitors from most countries may obtain an e-Visa for 90 days. Extension is possible for another 90 days. ... Citizens of the following countries are ineligible to obtain an e-Visa and must obtain a visa in advance: Afghanistan Bangladesh Cameroon Eritrea Ethiopia Ghana Guinea Haiti Iraq Kenya Nepal Nigeria Pakistan Philippines Sierra Leone Somalia Sri Lanka Syria Uzbekistan Yemen ... Entry and transit is refused for Kosovo nationals
